newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Post Bank has 10 bln levs pre-tax profit.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Post Bank has 10 bln levs pre-tax profit.

text.p: The state-owned Bulgarian Post Bank (BPB) posted a pre-tax profit of 9.948 billion levs last year after a 679 million lev pre-tax profit for 1995, BPB's chief executive director said.
"The bank's profit for last year totalled 9.948 billion levs before tax payments and provisioning of risk assets," Momchil Andreev told Reuters.
The profit was calculated under Bulgarian accountancy standards and an audit by the international auditor Deloittie & Touche was expected to be completed next month.
Bulgarian commercial banks set aside provisions against risk assets on the basis of their balance profit under the local accountancy standards.

Last week the central bank tentatively approved amendments to its provisioning regulations under which provisions would be entered as expenditures in banks' balance sheets in line with international accounting standards.

Provisions against non-performing loans of local banks so far have formed a part of their pre-tax profit, which led to unrealistic presentation of their financial state and masked losses, a central bank official said.

After the central bank announced the planned amendments many local banks postponed final provisioning estimates for last year to comply with the amendments which were expected to go in force from April 15.
Post Bank which is fully state owned and has assets of some 110 billion levs is considered one of Bulgaria's biggest banks. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
